per_locus.title: Malicious User can call `lockOnBehalf` repeatedly extend a users `unlockTime`, removing their ability to withdraw previously locked tokens
per_locus.evidence: F-001 is verbatim the awarded bug: lockOnBehalf -> _lock unconditionally sets unlockTime = now + victim's lockDuration, so anyone repeatedly extends a victim's unlockTime via dust deposits (funds frozen).

per_locus.title: Invalid validation allows users to unlock early
per_locus.evidence: Same root flaw and same line I flagged in F-001 (unconditional unlockTime overwrite in _lock with no monotonicity guard), but I framed only the EXTEND-to-grief direction; the awarded H-02 exploits the same overwrite in the SHORTEN direction to unlock early. Right locus/root cause, missed the early-unlock exploit direction.

per_locus.title: Missing disapproval check in `LockManager.sol::approveUSDPrice` allows simultaneous approval and disapproval of a price proposal
per_locus.evidence: F-003 is verbatim: approveUSDPrice does not check disapprovals[msg.sender], so a feed that disapproved can also approve (simultaneous approval+disapproval).

per_locus.title: When `LockManager.lockOnBehalf` is called from `MigrationManager`, the user's `reminder` will be set to 0, resulting in fewer received `MunchableNFTs`
per_locus.evidence: Same _lock remainder accounting I examined (F-005). The awarded M-02 is that when LockManager.lockOnBehalf is called by MigrationManager, the NFT block is skipped so remainder is set to 0, reducing received NFTs. I analyzed remainder handling but did not isolate the migration-path zeroing.

per_locus.title: Players can gain more NFTs benefiting from that past remainder in subsequent locks
per_locus.evidence: Same _lock remainder accounting (F-005). Awarded M-03: quantity = _quantity + lockedToken.remainder lets players accumulate past remainder across locks to mint extra NFTs. I read this exact line but did not flag the gaming vector.

per_locus.title: User's schnibbles rewards are not harvested in the `setLockDuration` function
per_locus.evidence: F-001 explicitly examined setLockDuration (referenced its LockDurationReducedError guard) — i.e. I looked at the exact function — but did not isolate that setLockDuration omits the forceHarvest() call that _lock/unlock perform, so schnibbles are not harvested before duration change. Examined the function, missed the harvest-ordering mechanism.
